chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: He narrated to me Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adamy said: He narrated to me a man, and Umar ibn Abdul-Aziz from Jamil ibn Durraj said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

The best of you are the generous ones, and the worst of you are the miserly ones. And among the good deeds is kindness to brothers, and striving to fulfill their needs. And in that is breaking the back of Satan, and moving away from the Fire and entering the Gardens. O Jamil! Inform the noble ones from your companions of this hadith. I said to him: May I be your ransom, who are the noble ones from my companions? He said: They are the kind ones to their brothers in hardship and ease.

Then he said: O Jamil! Indeed, for the owner of abundance, that is easy for him. And God, the Mighty and Exalted, praised the owner of little, saying: 'And they give preference over themselves, even though they are in poverty. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - those are the successful.'
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the best and worst people according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this hadith within the ethical framework of *al-khisal*, emphasizing that true generosity (*samah*) is tested by consistency in both ease and hardship, not merely by the capacity of the wealthy. The Imam links social solidarity—specifically fulfilling the needs of brothers—to spiritual victory over Satan, framing charitable giving as a practical means of escaping the Fire. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *birr* (piety) manifested through tangible social support, echoing the Quranic ideal of *ithar* (selflessness).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-42 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Sahl ibn Zyad al-Adamy, on the authority of someone and Umar ibn Abdul-Aziz, on the authority of Jamil ibn Dur’raj, “Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, ‘

The best of you are the generous ones, and the worst of you are the miserly ones. Being good is doing good deeds for your brethren and trying to fulfill their needs. Such deeds will debase Satan, free man from the Fire and take him into Paradise. O Jamil! Relate this to the noble ones from amongst your friends.’”Jamil ibn Dur’raj added, “I asked, ‘May I be your ransom! Who are the noble ones from amongst my friends?’ Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, ‘They are the ones who are good to their friends both in times of ease and in times of difficulty.’

Then Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) added, ‘O Jamil! This would be easy to do for one who is well-off. The Honorable the Exalted God has praised the act of doing good by those who have very little and has said, ‘… but give them preference over themselves, even though poverty was their (own lot). And those saved from the covetousness of their own souls,- they are the ones that achieve prosperity.’’ ”
